desc: Garry Nolan's laboratory in Stanford's Department of Pathology is an unlikely but decisive node in the custody chain. Its scientific business is systems immunology, cancer and cytometry - it co-developed CODEX and multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI) with Michael Angelo and Sean Bendall, techniques designed to map the spatial distribution of proteins and lanthanide-tagged markers in tissue at sub-cellular resolution. Those same instruments turn out to be near-ideal for interrogating an unknown metallic sample: MIBI resolved the Council Bluffs material at 200 nanometres laterally and in five-nanometre depth increments, alongside secondary ion mass spectrometry for elemental and isotopic composition. The laboratory is also where, on Nolan's own account to KQED in June 2021, representatives of the government and of an unnamed aerospace corporation brought a request to assess medical harm to individuals from 'supposed interactions with an anomalous craft', because of the blood analysis the laboratory could do. That is the significant fact: a university pathology laboratory, not a federal laboratory or an FFRDC, became the analytical destination for both alleged UAP material and alleged UAP casualty biology - which is exactly what you would expect if the holder needed analysis without generating a federal record.
